The study employed the Large-Eddy Simulation with Near-Wall Resolution (LES-NWR) to numerically simulate the turbulent free-shear flow over a prism at a Reynolds number of 22,000.
The computational grid consists of 4.3 million hexahedral elements, with 2.9 million elements in the refined region around the prism.
The wall-adjacent cell height was set to maintain a y+ less than unity, with 36 layers resolving the viscous sublayer.
The study investigated sampling ranges from 2,000 to 23,000 snapshots and sampling resolutions from 50 to 105 Hz.
The Stabilization state, identified as the optimal state for modal convergence, occurs when the DMD output becomes independent of the sampling range.
The study found that the convergence of the sampling range and resolution are mutually independent.
Over-sampling, where the temporal dimension, n, approaches and transcends the spatial dimension, m (i.e., m < n), leads to algorithmic instability and divergence of the DMD output.
The recommended sampling resolution of 15 frames per cycle for target activities is suggested for most engineering implementations.
The study invested over 800,000 core-hours, excluding the LES-NWR simulation, to complete the comprehensive parametric investigation.
The turbulent free-shear flow over a prism was chosen as the test case due to its simplicity, sophistication, and relevance to a wide range of engineering applications.
